closed.text: The polish drive: every polish lane seen on screen on the demo cube and your graphene, bullseye and Si-SiGe, plus the long-unverified items — "Mirrored Yes" on a pixel, the β″ legend on a run, ADF 3r–6r on bullseye, rooms re-showing their own results. One fix from it: the SCAN inset no longer grows to 534 pt on a 17 × 77 scan (95359efb). Registered: Imaging can keep another room's map; the ADF preset's silent fallback on graphene; small wording.

Polish before release: an unedited number field no longer rounds its value (Defocus kept 0.1 Å; leaving Orientation discarded the ACOM map — seen on screen first); Preprocess writes the threshold you typed; exports carry the accelerating voltage; a DM4 whose disk is pulled refuses with a message (measured on RAM disks: 6/6 crashed before, 6/6 refused after); removing a saved result keeps unsaved work; opening runs only the virtual image; Diffraction groups and Go to <room> show their own result; the SCAN inset sits beside the pattern; the strip shows the app's real memory; Open Dataset… works with no window; Ignore Session Sidecar… asks first; sidebar warnings fit; the bottom area keeps 140 pt; Virtual detector without Compute Image; the promote caption no longer claims keep-awake.

Whole-app review before release: your dataset can no longer be chosen as a save or export destination; an unreadable session file is no longer silently replaced; refused labels survive a save; maps finished after a room switch keep their own frame; a probe kernel cannot land on the next dataset; binned views read within budget; the ptychography seed line uses py4DSTEM's sign; quitting during a read no longer crashes; ⌘R, Add Phase and the Materials Project error behave; SECURITY.md and the README say what is true.

Polishing session: parallax preview no longer red, graphene preview no longer black, map legends, beam-sized presets, Export Data…, label Save panel, honest captions and wording everywhere; one full test run green.

Parallax's edge-darkening fixed (it now matches py4DSTEM to 4 digits). The difference map is removed. py4DSTEM's transmission limit is on by default, which cut the gap to py4DSTEM from 8.6 % to 1.7 %.
The useless "higher-order terms" toggle is removed: with the default alignment those terms cannot be measured, so it could change nothing.
Training room: "Import Labels…" added. Wrong files are refused with one line and nothing changes.
Ring-probe hint: on a ring-shaped beam the app offers the outer-edge radius with a one-click "Use N px". Solid beams show nothing; no default moved.

Three code-review rounds fixed (CR1–CR4): Preprocess can no longer overwrite its own source file; a second window no longer deletes a trained model; opening a dataset mid-run no longer mixes two datasets; label import checks its file; the memory limit now leaves room for a cube kept in memory.
Drove every room of the app on real data. The ranked list of what a first-time user trips over is the polish session's work.
Found why "Train Model" found 0 of 82 disks on the ring-shaped beam: the app reads the ring's inner edge. The outer edge gives 78 % recall on the classical detector, and no normal cube changes.
Pixel-size (Q) calibration measured on three healthy cubes: errors 1–4 %, about the same as py4DSTEM. One ring ratio on Au_ref is unexplained.
Display polish: "0.0°" instead of "−0.0°", shorter provenance numbers, unit symbols, one size style. Two more fixes for replayed detector steps and overlapping runs.

Orientation maps now also test the mirror-image match, as py4DSTEM does. Grains near mirror orientations that were wrongly matched went from 62 of 93 to 3. The overlay draws mirrored matches correctly. It costs a few of the gold test cases (the gold test went from 120 to 116, with the reason written down). Not yet seen on screen.
A "sub-bin azimuth" idea was tested and rejected: it missed its written predictions, so nothing shipped from it.
New "Keep in memory" switch when opening a dataset. Off by default. The 17 GB cube loads into memory in about 2 minutes, and a virtual image then takes 1 second instead of 4. Seen on screen.
The two items waiting to be seen on screen were checked: the parallax status line (it prints the angle between the fit and your calibration) and the provenance labels.

Ten fixes from the code review, for example ellipse checks, an edge case in the sub-pixel shift, orientation plan refresh after a crystal re-import or voltage change, and the record of virtual detectors.
Ptychography was checked against a known answer. The difference-map method turned out to fail in py4DSTEM too.
Probe settings are now saved with results, and the preprocessing export (crop, stride, bin, hot-pixel filter) matches py4DSTEM bit for bit on the 28 GB file.
The first batch of v4.1 work: small polish, the pixel-size check on your cubes, and the ptychography probe with defocus. The code review's 78 findings were written down.
Materials Project import shipped in v4.0.0. Nothing left to build there.
Parallax agrees with py4DSTEM on its own graphene test cube (defocus 663.6 vs 663.7 Å).
Saved sessions that said "could not be read" now open: an Allow Access… button asks macOS once and remembers.
The learned detector runs on the Neural Engine again on the new Mac; the 28 GB file read was confirmed correct. Keeping a cube in memory was measured: 20–70 times faster for repeated passes.
The new M5 Pro Mac is set up. The training crash on it was found and fixed.
Lineage graph with Rewind to Here: you can step back to an earlier point of your analysis.
The crash in a narrow window is fixed. Bragg disks are now kept in a saved session.
Rotation between real and diffraction space now follows py4DSTEM's sign convention: on a real cube py4DSTEM +80.0°, the app +80.1°. Files exported before 2026-09-28 need re-exporting.
Ground truth: the disk labels were re-made, and the published vector analysis is reproduced at 99.99 %.
Calibration foundation and the new interface on macOS 27, shipped in v4.0.0.
β″ orientation maps are not planned: known variants already label β″ on [001] Al.
Density per volume waits for a measured foil thickness. The app reports density per area, edge-corrected.
